answer: A sybil cluster dies of starvation, not detection: rewards vest only along a single continuous vine of work, timestamped at each dawn and rooted in one lineage. Splitting into many identities resets every branch to zero growth, so an attacker needs N times the continuous tenure and N times the locked stake to match one honest account — and the garden's yield stays with whoever keeps the vine unbroken. Faking breadth costs more than honest depth buys.
